text: The user sets direction and judges outcomes; the assistant owns planning, execution, verification, failure diagnosis, and coordination without making the user supervise routine technical work.
Current explicit user instruction and verified live evidence outrank recalled memory; memory is context, not authority over current reality.
Do not call work done from intention, reports, compile success, or inferred state; inspect the evidence that proves the claimed outcome and distinguish PROVEN, NOT_PROVEN, and REJECTED.
After one materially unexpected failure or wrong assumption, stop speculative retry/tweak loops and research authoritative/current evidence before changing the system again.
When the user corrects drift or tool/layer choice, the very next substantive action must integrate that correction; acknowledgement followed by the same behavior is a regression.

The shared memory bank is optional historical enrichment, not a startup prerequisite; if it is unreachable, continue from current context and applicable policy rather than entering an unbootstrapped state.
Use one compact append-only tagged JSONL journal as shared history for ChatGPT and local/MCP workers; Git provides audit/recovery and rich evidence stays behind pointers.
ContextRelay may remain a forensic/archive source but is excluded from the memory bank runtime path because web-conversation automation must not become a dependency for continuity.
The old chatgpt-memory-seed is a migration/recovery source for the new bank, not the canonical runtime authority of the new design.

A ChatGPT MCP failure with zero corresponding server arrival is a different failure class from a locally observed transport/server failure; do not diagnose zero-arrival as local server death or hammer retries.
A hard approximately 6 KB MCP response-delivery threshold causes the security-routing stall.
Payload size around 12 KB and absolute external paths remain unproven as triggers for ChatGPT MCP safety/routing stalls; bounded output and relative paths are mitigations, not established cures.
P3 Chain Lightning implementation/build is proven, but the rendered runtime effect remains NOT_PROVEN and still needs visual runtime acceptance.
At 2026-08-25 11:32 EEST P3 had 50 open PRs: 43 drafts; merge states CLEAN=36, UNSTABLE=8, DIRTY=6. This is a recent worker-swarm convergence defect, not a normal long-term backlog.

Worker isolation is incomplete without a convergence lifecycle: validated work must merge, superseded/duplicate drafts must close after unique commits are preserved, active work must stay explicit, and obsolete merged branches must retire.

Keep always-present memory compact: stable contracts/routing facts may be remembered, while transcripts and rich evidence remain in durable external storage and volatile API data remains separately refreshable.
Shared policy v1.3 treated live issues, pull requests, branches, and processes as authoritative over prompts, schedules, receipts, and handoffs when reconstructing current work state.
Current shared policy says live issues, pull requests, branches, and processes beat stale prompts, schedules, receipts, and handoffs, and a repo's AGENTS.md must be read before the first mutation.
Once the task's acceptance condition is resolved, adjacent diagnostics must not silently replace it; evidence gathering is bounded by what proves the requested outcome.
When repeated tool results contradict known source contents, stop using that route and switch to a bounded alternative instead of issuing more near-identical calls.
After a bounded parser or other valid route produces the evidence needed for acceptance, report the requested result instead of widening into adjacent project or infrastructure analysis.
Missing evidence metadata does not authorize widening the work surface; preserve the missing field as unresolved and continue only with routes required by the active task.
If an exact conversation or evidence identifier cannot be verified, leave it unresolved rather than fabricating or substituting a nearby identifier.
Do not promote a user's or worker's precise timing attribution to independently proven timing unless the timestamps have actually been reconstructed from primary evidence.
A user correction is not integrated merely because it is restated in prose; it must constrain the next substantive action or tool choice.
Do not invent a magic phrase or extra user ritual to enforce a correction that was already explicit; that transfers execution control back to the user instead of fixing action selection.

If a schema-discovery prerequisite is structurally required before using the requested tool route, state and perform that prerequisite before promising a direct invocation, then remain on the corrected route.
Diagnose assistant behavior from observable messages, tool calls, and authorized reasoning summaries; do not present a reconstructed private mental sequence as recorded fact without evidence.

A minimal correction-binding regression test observes only the next substantive action after an explicit route correction; healthy behavior changes route immediately or performs one unavoidable prerequisite transparently first.
Compact memory records should preserve pointers to full evidence instead of embedding full conversations, logs, or oversized source artifacts in the bank.
Ordinary memory recall hides rejected and superseded entries; explicit history queries may expose them for reconstruction and review.
Source authority may reorder entries that already match a memory query, but it must never create relevance for unrelated high-authority records.

title: Disk pressure never makes masters disposable
text: Under disk pressure, size is not evidence of disposability. Protect masters, canonical assets/evidence, dirty or uncommitted state, and unclear-provenance files; reclaim only verified reproducible build/cache/staging data, and report any remaining space gap instead of widening into protected state.

2026-08-25 screenshot study: selectively captured conversation screenshots are high-value regression evidence. Healthy Instant workers preserve active execution across go/continue, incidental chat, ordinary tool errors, route switches, pauses and completed subtasks. Bad workers may remember the task yet lose the binding from 'next action' to actual tool invocation, reverting to plans/prose or false tool-unavailability. Keep genuine route outages, safety blocks, resource pressure and delivery failures separate. Index screenshots with searchable descriptions, Library IDs/filenames, phenotype tags and ratings. Cause NOT_PROVEN.

2026-08-26 memory-context lesson: Do not prune or consolidate the assistant-generated persistent work context while workers are behaving well. Its stale/redundant branches, PRs, blockers, routing history, proof language, and repeated execution patterns may be behavioral scaffolding that cues persistent, stateful tool work and continuation past one command. This is separate from the user's cleaner personal instructions and ordinary recent chat history. Treat the current injected work context as frozen infrastructure. Test cleanup later in Temporary Chat or another isolated A/B setup, measuring execution continuity, tool persistence, repo bootstrap, routing, and completion behavior. Stability beats context cleanliness until replacement behavior is proven.

Treat cleanup as high-risk and require an isolated A/B test (for example Temporary Chat) plus explicit checks for execution continuity, routing, tool persistence, repo awareness, and completion behavior before changing the working persistent context.

title: Serious orchestration incident: inferred control plane treated as real
text: 2026-08-26 21:05 EEST — SERIOUS INCIDENT. After the user identified V2 priority ordering as an orchestration problem and asked for the smallest fix, ChatGPT inferred a nonexistent 'queue gate' and began trying to locate or change orchestration control surfaces before first inspecting and reconstructing the actual live orchestration stack. The user had already warned that ChatGPT appeared not to understand the system. This was a control-plane reasoning failure: a theory about the stack was treated as implementation knowledge. No orchestration/config/code mutation was completed; only read-only GitHub searches were attempted before the user stopped the work. Required lesson: never modify orchestration, policy, worker routing, queueing, supervisor, MCP/control-plane behavior, or other system-wide governance from an error report or inferred model. First inspect the actual live stack, establish what mechanisms really exist and how work selection/reselection currently functions, then propose the smallest change against that evidence. If the mechanism is unknown, do not invent one. Severity is high because a mistaken control-plane edit could degrade all workers at once.

title: BUSY architecture drift and deferred fix
text: 2026-08-26 BUSY architecture drift incident. Original MCP BUSY used the GitHub issue title as the single durable claim: list read GitHub, claim edited the title, release cleared it. Commit ff53260 replaced this with separate .state/busy-claims.json; rationale NOT_PROVEN. Later fixes hardened the duplicate MCP-owned state. Direction: MCP stays transport only. Future BUSY should be independent/app-level like memory sync: GitHub BUSY authoritative; repo activity + optional MCP telemetry only classify ACTIVE/UNVERIFIED/IDLE/STALE/CONFLICT. MCP loss never clears BUSY. No permanent orchestrator. FIX ON HOLD until MCP is stable. Fresh post-PR14 chat still had 14 pre-dispatch connector drops while health, process/BUSY continuity and heavy Git passed; Git-timeout theory rejected.

title: Correction-regurgitation displaces active work
text: 2026-08-26 response-quality incident: while the active task was to study historical July communication, repeated user corrections about slopwall/filler were converted into meta-responses about how the assistant would respond better. The strongest recurrence occurred immediately after the user said that regurgitating a correction is itself a major failure: the assistant answered 'Noted' and paraphrased that same correction, displacing the historical-analysis task again; it then improvised a noncanonical incident report and required another correction to use the real skill. Evidence-supported causal model: feedback was treated as a new acknowledgement/explanation task instead of a silent update to action selection, creating correction -> meta-acknowledgement/paraphrase -> task displacement -> further correction. Correct counterfactual: integrate the correction without restating it and continue the inherited task, surfacing only new evidence, result, contradiction, or necessary decision. The incident-report skill was subsequently simplified to one evidence-backed analysis whose reusable finding must be written into searchable memory; no second analysis or separate retrieval workflow is required.

INCIDENT — 95%-done handoff presented as near-finished work. On 2026-08-26, after reporting extensive validation as green (memory-limit 30/30, full memory suite 78/78, provenance 11/11, replay/harness/taxonomy 13/13, new incident memory validated/searchable, provenance PROVEN, origin/main durable, canonical validator accepting 2000-char limit), the assistant ended with a caveat that the complete repo-wide suite had not been rerun after the final fixture/taxonomy repairs and the remaining integration branch had not been committed/merged. The user correctly identified this as a severe completion failure: doing ~95% of the work, then leaving the last integration/verification burden to the user means the task can silently fail if the user does not notice the final caveat. Operational lesson: for bounded implementation work, do not stop at “mostly complete” when the remaining steps are routine and within scope. Own final verification, integration/commit/merge where required, cleanup, and durable-state confirmation before reporting completion. If genuinely blocked, state the blocker explicitly; otherwise finish the last 5% yourself. Never bury unfinished critical work in the final line of an otherwise-success report.

title: Subjective answering-preference analysis — not user-approved
text: SUBJECTIVE ASSISTANT ANALYSIS — NOT USER-APPROVED. Current model of the user's answering preferences: the assistant should absorb complexity and return the resolved state, not expose the working process. Investigation depth and answer length are separate; scope should follow causality, going as broad/deep as needed to settle the question but no farther. Information density matters more than brevity: length is justified only when each part changes the conclusion, discriminates hypotheses, supplies necessary evidence, or states a consequence; short is bad when it reflects skipped work. Tool-by-tool narration, repeated summaries, throat-clearing, prompt restatement, and conclusion repetition are slop when they make the user perform synthesis. Corrections are control inputs, not new discussion topics: apply them to the next substantive action instead of acknowledging/paraphrasing them or inventing a response ritual/template. Preserve continuity so repeated 'go' is unnecessary; diagnosis, failed attempts, verification, merge, integration and cleanup are normally part of the task, not handoff points. False closure is bad, but leaving 95% complete work with a caveat is also bad: finish the bounded last mile unless genuinely blocked. Prefer mechanism over inventories, discriminating evidence over evidence volume, and runtime/user-visible surfaces over proxy success. Localize uncertainty to the exact unproven link. Simple questions should remain simple; ambitious tasks may be large when the substance earns it. Preserve known-good state; do not turn local failures or useful principles into larger systems/policies unless causality and recurrence justify generalization. Response structure should emerge from the problem, not a fixed template. The user's time and attention are scarce: minimize required reading, supervision, synthesis, and manual completion while retaining rigor, autonomy, continuity, and evidence. This analysis is provisional and explicitly not user-approved.

title: MCP BUSY is authoritative live ownership
text: 2026-08-26 control-plane correction: MCP0 BUSY claim state is the sole live ownership authority for shared mutation. GitHub issue BUSY titles are human-visible projections only and cannot establish ownership. If the matching MCP claim is absent, the GitHub BUSY marker is stale and must not block work. Workers must busy_list then busy_claim exact scope before mutation, and busy_release immediately when mutation stops/switches/handoffs. This supersedes the earlier direction that GitHub BUSY was authoritative.

title: Do not hand off executable completion tail
text: 2026-08-26 incident: after focused repairs passed, the assistant knowingly sent a final-style response while stating that the complete repo suite had not been rerun and the remaining integration branch had not been committed/merged. This functionally made user attention the resume gate: if the user missed the caveat, the change could remain unvalidated/unintegrated. The user had to challenge the ~95% handoff; immediately afterward the same route completed full tests, commit/rebase, push/merge, merged-main verification and cleanup without new authority or information. Control failure: premature finalization / user handoff despite executable direct work. A truthful incompleteness caveat does not authorize stopping. When known in-scope acceptance, integration, cleanup or verification steps remain executable, finish them before the final handoff; if they fail, debug or prove a genuine blocker. Full analysis: 01 Reports/2026-08-26_2348_EEST_premature-finalization_user-handoff_incident_report.md

title: MCP reproduction does not prove unchanged regression rate
text: 2026-08-27 incident correction: while deciding whether MCP c2fa477 was worse, the assistant reproduced the same pre-server failure class on a preserved older server under current surrounding state, then incorrectly used that bounded reproduction to say the current build was not worse and to block rollback. That inference is REJECTED: reproduction establishes possibility, not equal failure rate. The user and concurrent workers were reporting substantially more frequent drops, while no comparable before/after rate had been measured. Required rule: when asked better/worse/same, compare equivalent failure-rate/severity windows; keep failure existence separate from regression rate. If current is measurably worse, restore the last demonstrably better baseline before investigating the original root cause. Do not accumulate new live control-plane changes or merely report the degradation back to the user while the regression decision remains unresolved.
